source.display_title: 05/12/2026 - Grant Childress x Farooq Bey  — Closed

prospect.name: Grant Childress
prospect.location: Tyler, Texas, USA — about ninety minutes from Dallas
prospect.occupation: Financial advisor, building his own practice; client-facing
prospect.family_status: Married; wife wants to return to yoga. One child, Cooper, four months old. Chocolate labrador.
prospect.training_background: College football player, in peak condition at around 190 lb and 8-10% body fat, which he rates a nine or ten out of ten. Rates himself five or six today. Back in the gym doing olympic-style lifting but conditioning has collapsed — 'I go through two sets of clean snatches, I'm sucking wind.' Has followed Trevor's content for a while and used his workouts independently. Makes periodic restart attempts that burn out.
prospect.medical: Reports back problems attributed to old sports injuries, with pain on everyday movement — 'from old sports injuries, you know, I feel like I have bad back issues, know, just moving around... I just feel like I'm not hurting just to move around.' No diagnosis, imaging, treating clinician or duration was established, because no question was asked about it.

signals: Already in reasonable shape and explicit that this is not a rescue — 'I'm not, you know, terribly out of shape. I just want to get back to my peak shape again'
Price registered as no barrier at all: asked how payment works before hearing a number, heard $6,000 and $9,000, and chose a tier without a single question about cost

Successful professional who deliberately traded fitness for business building rather than losing it to illness or injury — 'I've been so focused on work and building my business. It's just, I've kind of let that side of my life go'
Minor rebuilder colouring in the language ('get back to where I was') but no regret, no hard season, and a self-directed athlete's confidence: 'I know what I can do, I know where I was'

goals.text: Get from 208 lb back to around 190 and cut the midsection
Rebuild endurance and conditioning, which he names as his biggest current downfall
Make health a priority so his four-month-old son grows up seeing it — 'I want to be able to set an example in that way'
Bring more fire and intensity into the office and to client-facing work
Move better and stop hurting in everyday movement — 'I want to feel like I move better mobility and just feel like I'm not hurting just to move around'
A week-to-week game plan for training and nutrition so nothing falls through the cracks
Get fit alongside his wife, who wants to return to yoga, and keep each other accountable

pains.text: Back problems from old sports injuries causing pain in ordinary movement
Conditioning has collapsed since college — 'two sets of clean snatches, something like that, I'm just, you know, I'm sucking wind'

Falls apart without external instruction — 'I operate a lot better when I have someone giving me instructions and I have a game plan in front of me. But when it's just myself, things can fall through the cracks'
Restart attempts burn out because he does too much at once — 'I try to jump into it 100%, whereas I probably should gradually ease myself into it'
Three to five years of letting fitness slide while building the business
Without a plan he defers — 'I get home, I'm like, well, what am I doing today? I don't really know. So I might just put it off for the next day'
Nutrition not yet structured; trying to build meal prep on his own
Carrying what he calls a dad bod and a pudge in the midsection

offer.guarantee_mentioned: On extending mid-programme: 'If, if after the six months you said, heck, I want to do another six, we won't charge you another 6k. We just charge you the difference.'

evidence: Chose the tier without hesitation: 'I would say six months because I know, mean, once I dive into it, I mean, I think I can, I'll get fired up into it pretty quick'
Explicit agreement to proceed — 'happy to move forward' / 'Yeah, absolutely' / 'Awesome. Let's do it'
Rep moved straight into onboarding: 'Okay. So I'll just walk you through the next steps now'
No objection of any kind was raised at any point in the call, on price or anything else

Counter-evidence, and why confidence is 0.85: payment is not witnessed. The transcript ends at 'First, I'll remove my Fathom note-taker. Obviously, we're taking personal information here.' No link, no confirmation, no Trevor booking and no agreement signing appear on the record.
outcome.next_step: Process payment, then a one-on-one onboarding call with Trevor, initial movement patterns, and a programme designed within three days.

notable.note: The fastest and cleanest close in the batch — 18 minutes, zero objections, sanctioned pricing only — and the only prospect who matches every stated ICP criterion. It is also a call where the entire baseline phase was skipped, and that omission has a cost here: at 00:13:36 the prospect volunteered 'from old sports injuries, you know, I feel like I have bad back issues, know, just moving around' and 'I just feel like I'm not hurting just to move around', and the rep asked nothing at all — not what the injury was, not how long, not whether anyone has looked at it — answering instead with the generic line about being designed to be fluid, then closing him on a six-month kettlebell programme minutes later. The rep also explicitly noticed and enjoyed how easy the call was: 'Thanks for making my life easy, Grant. You know, some people you really have to kind of challenge politely on these conversations.' The consequence frame was effectively skipped on that basis. Recording was again stopped at the payment step, so no close in this rep's corpus is verifiable from the transcript.

quality.notes: Heavy inversion, and it is worst at the close — 'happy to move forward', 'Yeah, absolutely' and 'Awesome. Let's do it' are distributed across both labels in a way that cannot be literally correct. The rep's own questions ('How can we potentially help you?', 'Any questions, thoughts you want to add to that, concerns?') repeatedly sit under the prospect's label, and the prospect's answers under the rep's. Roles assigned from content. Prospect joined as 'Grant's iPhone' rather than a named account. Several short passages are garbled beyond recovery.
